title: White Dwarfs: Stellar Remnants and Electron Degeneracy

key_sections.title: 1. Electron Degeneracy Pressure
key_sections.content:
White dwarfs generate no nuclear fusion energy. They are held in hydrostatic equilibrium against gravitational collapse by electron degeneracy pressure, a quantum mechanical effect governed by the Pauli Exclusion Principle. Understanding this phenomenon requires analyzing the underlying thermodynamic, gravitational, and electromagnetic forces at play. Modern scientific observations using space telescopes, orbital sensors, and computer simulations continue to refine theoretical models, resolving long-standing questions regarding energy transport, structural stability, and cosmic evolution across varying observational scales.

White dwarfs represent the final evolutionary endpoint for over 97% of stars in the Milky Way. After exhausting core hydrogen and helium fusion, stars with masses up to 8 solar masses shed their outer gas layers to form planetary nebulae, leaving behind dense carbon-oxygen cores.

key_sections.title: 2. The Chandrasekhar Limit
key_sections.content:
The maximum mass limit for a stable white dwarf is approximately 1.4 solar masses. If a white dwarf accretes enough material from a companion star to exceed this limit, it triggers a catastrophic thermonuclear detonation known as a Type Ia Supernova.
